title: China's PBOC lifts FX reserve ratio to 6%: what it means for the yuan, AUD
body: The move signals that Beijing is uncomfortable with the pace of the yuan's recent strength. That gives USD/CNY and USD/CNH a floor near current levels rather than reversing the trend outright. Its direct liquidity effect is modest, so traders are likely to treat it as a warning shot, with the daily fixing the main tool to watch for follow-through. The signal reaches beyond China: a PBOC leaning against appreciation tends to temper gains in other Asian currencies that trade alongside the yuan, such as the Korean won and Taiwan dollar. It can also weigh at the margin on the Australian dollar, which often trades as a China proxy. The timing matters too, with the US dollar already softer on Iran diplomacy hopes. If the dollar weakens further, the PBOC may need stronger signals to hold the line. --- Earlier: China's central bank, regulators to meet on stock support after record 12-week slide --- China's central bank is making dollars scarcer onshore to take some heat out of a strengthening yuan, a modest move in size but a clear signal of where Beijing wants the currency to go.

title: PBOC is expected to set the USD/CNY reference rate at 6.6489 – Reuters estimate
body: The People's Bank of China is due to set the daily USD/CNY reference rate at around 0115 GMT (2115 US Eastern time), a fixing that remains one of the most closely watched signals in Asian foreign exchange markets. China operates a managed floating exchange rate system, under which the renminbi (yuan) is allowed to trade within a prescribed band around a central reference rate, or midpoint, set each trading day by the PBOC. The current trading band permits the currency to move plus or minus 2% from the official midpoint during onshore trading hours. Each morning, the PBOC determines the midpoint based on a range of inputs. These include the previous day's closing price, movements in major currencies, particularly the US dollar, broader international FX conditions, and domestic economic considerations such as capital flows, growth momentum and financial stability objectives. The midpoint is not a purely mechanical calculation, allowing policymakers discretion to guide market expectations. Once the midpoint is announced, onshore USD/CNY is free to trade within the allowable band. If market pressures push the yuan toward either edge of that range, the central bank may step in to smooth volatility. Intervention can take the form of direct buying or selling of yuan, adjustments to liquidity conditions, or guidance through state-owned banks. As a result, the daily fixing is often interpreted as a policy signal rather than just a technical reference point.

title: CIA chief Ratcliffe reportedly advises Trump to keep 'no war, no deal' pressure on Iran
body: For oil, the advice points to a prolonged standoff rather than a resolution. That keeps Iranian supply constrained with no near-term prospect of a deal returning barrels to the market. The "no war" element in principle limits the tail risk of a full-scale conflict that could disrupt shipping through the Strait of Hormuz. However, today's reports of blasts on Qeshm Island and claims of limited US strikes show that low-level military friction is continuing. Ratcliffe's view that economic pain could trigger internal unrest adds a further, harder-to-price risk, since instability inside Iran could itself threaten production and exports. The net effect is likely to keep a geopolitical risk premium embedded in crude rather than build or remove it sharply. - Earlier: Up to six blasts reported near Iran's Qeshm Island as Israeli TV cites US strike - The CIA director is reportedly advising Trump to let economic pressure do the work on Iran, betting that sustained pain will bring either concessions or upheaval.

title: US midterms: what traders need to know as narrow Congress majorities face voters
body: For markets, the main question is whether Washington's fiscal path continues or stalls. A Democratic win in either chamber would likely bring legislative gridlock on that agenda, a shift toward cost-of-living measures covering healthcare, housing and energy, and a heavier load of congressional investigations, adding headline risk. Possible legal challenges over how the vote is administered could also extend uncertainty beyond election night, a risk for volatility in equities and the dollar if results are contested. --- US election: The key races that could tip control of Congress --- Control of Congress hinges on a handful of seats in Tuesday's US midterms, and the result will shape whether the current fiscal agenda carries on or runs into a divided Washington.

title: Philippines Factory Activity Contracts for 2nd Month
body: The S&P Global Philippines Manufacturing PMI slipped to 49.1 in October 2026 from 49.6 in September, signaling a second consecutive month of contraction as both output and new orders continued to decline. Although the pace of output reduction slowed, the drop in new orders intensified, with firms attributing weaker demand to subdued market conditions and unusually hot weather, which some associated with El Niño. New export orders also fell, albeit modestly. Manufacturers scaled back purchasing activity further, with the decline reaching its sharpest pace in 11 months, while employment contracted for the second month in a row. Supplier delivery times lengthened for the 11th consecutive month. Pre-production inventories were broadly unchanged, but stocks of finished goods edged up for the first time in four months. Despite the muted operating environment, business confidence improved, climbing to its highest level in nearly two years. At the same time, price pressures softened, as input costs registered their slowest rate of increase in eight months. The material has been provided by InstaForex Company - www.instaforex.com

title: South Korea Inflation Slows in October
body: South Korea's annual inflation rate eased for the second straight month, slipping to 2.8% in October 2026 from 2.9% in September. This was the lowest rate since July and came in below market expectations of 2.9%. Nevertheless, inflation remained above the central bank's 2% target, largely due to higher transport costs, which jumped 6.8% year-on-year, and a 5.1% increase in recreation and culture prices. Food and lodging prices rose 3%, while household goods and services were up 4%. Price gains in other categories were more subdued: alcoholic beverages and tobacco were unchanged, and groceries and non-alcoholic beverages inched up 0.5%. On a monthly basis, consumer prices increased 0.2% in October, falling short of the 0.3% forecast and slowing from the 0.3% rise recorded in the previous month. Meanwhile, core inflation, which excludes volatile food and energy items, climbed 2.8% from a year earlier and 0.4% from the previous month. title: WTI Crude Oil futures fall 8% as geopolitical risk premium fades.
body: WTI Crude Oil futures experienced heavy selling pressure, falling nearly 8% to trade around $96.30. The sharp drop comes after prices hit a five-and-a-half-month high in the previous session. The primary driver of the selloff was reported diplomatic progress between the U.S. and Iran, which helped reduce the risk premium in the crude market. The broader energy sector also faced downward pressure, with Natural Gas futures and RBOB gasoline joining the decline as prices fell across the board.

title: Live Cattle futures held steady as cash prices fell.
body: Live Cattle futures traded steady as declining cash prices and boxed beef values countered bullish market fundamentals, with the December contract falling $5.82 to $227.95. Feeder Cattle futures rebounded following Friday's month-end selling, pushing the January contract up $2.90 to $334.67 amid expectations of tightening supplies. Lean Hog futures traded sideways for a fourth consecutive session, despite a $41 million USDA purchase aimed at providing market relief. Meanwhile, money managers pushed Lean Hog net short positions to a record high of over 51,000 contracts.

title: Nasdaq-100 futures hit 3-month low on tech sector selling pressure.
body: Nasdaq-100 futures dropped over 1.5% to near 28,120, marking a third consecutive lower session and hitting their lowest level since July. The selling pressure is largely driven by concerns over artificial intelligence spending and cautious future earnings guidance from major tech companies, prompting market participants to question tech valuations. Meanwhile, the broader market showed dispersion as E-mini Dow futures posted gains amidst a sector rotation, while E-mini S&P 500 futures fell 0.5%.

title: Soybean futures reach recent lows as harvest pressure persists.
body: Soybean futures traded lower as harvest pressure and falling oil prices pushed the January contract down 16'6 to 1205'4. Corn futures consolidated in a tight range, finding some support as the harvest nears completion, while call option open interest reached 614,000 contracts. Wheat futures held steady, with the December Chicago contract staying above the 600'0 mark as lower prices attracted global buyers. Option open interest in wheat showed strong participation, adding 3,000 contracts to push call open interest to 188,000. Market participants await upcoming election results for further direction across the grain complex.
